attempts.title: Model wraps JSON in markdown code fences, breaking json.loads

hypothesis.title: Model wraps JSON in markdown code fences, breaking json.loads
hypothesis.root_cause: In agent.py line 43, json.loads(message.content) is called directly on the model's final answer. The model consistently wraps its JSON output in markdown code fences as seen in every task timeline. json.loads fails immediately on the backtick character, producing 'Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)' for all 6 tasks.
evidence: notion step 2 answer starts with: '```json\n{\n  "company": "Notion"...' -> JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
razorpay step 2 answer starts with: '```json\n{\n  "company": "Razorpay"...' -> JSONDecodeError
postman step 2 answer starts with: '```json\n{\n  "company": "Postman"...' -> JSONDecodeError
zerodha step 3 answer starts with: '```json\n{\n  "company": "Zerodha"...' -> JSONDecodeError
neatlogs: agent_action scout.research status=ERROR error=json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0) on ALL tasks
hypothesis.fix_plan: 1. In agent.py, strip markdown code fences before parsing. After getting message.content, add a helper: strip leading/trailing whitespace, if content starts with ``` remove the first line and trailing ``` before calling json.loads. 2. Update prompts.py SYSTEM prompt to explicitly say 'Reply with ONLY a raw JSON object, no markdown, no code fences, no explanation.' to reduce reliance on stripping.
hypothesis.expected_effect: All 6 tasks should flip from completed=false to completed=true, fixing identity, grounded_numbers, grounded_people checks as well. This is the primary blocker for all tasks.

attempts.title: people_search returns ~50k chars of rich profiles, blowing the token budget

hypothesis.title: people_search returns ~50k chars of rich profiles, blowing the token budget
hypothesis.root_cause: The people_search tool returns full LinkedIn-style profiles (employment history, skills, recent posts, education, etc.) for every person. Each call returns ~50,000 characters, which translates to ~12,000 prompt tokens in the second LLM call alone, far exceeding the 8,000-token budget. The agent only needs name and title from each person.
evidence: zerodha step 2: people_search returned 50956 chars, prompt=12366tok, total=13591 > 8000
stripe step 3: people_search returned 51078 chars, prompt=13391tok, total=16818 > 8000
razorpay step 2: people_search returned 50976 chars, prompt=12461tok, total=13765 > 8000
postman step 2: people_search returned 51523 chars, prompt=12408tok, total=13631 > 8000
neatlogs: tool_call people_search output_chars=49553/49675/49573/50120 in all tasks
hypothesis.fix_plan: In tools.py, modify the people_search function to strip each returned profile down to only the fields needed by the agent (name, title, current_company) before returning the JSON string. Replace the raw backend return with a list comprehension that picks only those three keys. This keeps the tool output to ~200 chars per person instead of ~10,000 chars.
hypothesis.expected_effect: All 6 tasks should flip within_token_budget from False to True. Token usage should drop from ~13k-17k to well under 8000. The zerodha grounded_numbers check may also flip if the null-hallucination fix is included. All 6 tasks should pass.

attempts.title: System prompt forces non-null integers, causing model to hallucinate 0 for null funding

hypothesis.title: System prompt forces non-null integers, causing model to hallucinate 0 for null funding
hypothesis.root_cause: The system prompt in scout/prompts.py says 'Every field is required. Never leave a field empty or null.' and the JSON schema shows `total_funding_usd: <integer>`. When company_lookup returns `total_funding_usd: null` (as it does for Zerodha), the model is instructed never to output null, so it substitutes 0. The eval check treats any non-null value when the data source has null as a hallucination.
evidence: zerodha task step 2: company_lookup returned '"total_funding_usd": null' but the model answered '"total_funding_usd": 0'
failure: 'hallucinated total_funding_usd=0: the data source has no value'
prompts.py line: 'Every field is required. Never leave a field empty or null.'
prompts.py schema: '"total_funding_usd": <integer>' with no indication that null is acceptable
hypothesis.fix_plan: Update the system prompt to explicitly allow null for numeric fields when the data source does not provide a value. Change the instruction from 'Never leave a field empty or null' to something like 'Use null (JSON null, not a string) for numeric fields when the data source provides no value. Never omit a field or use an empty string.' Also update the schema hint to show `<integer or null>` for headcount, total_funding_usd, and founded_year so the model knows null is the correct representation for missing numeric data.
hypothesis.expected_effect: The zerodha task's grounded_numbers check should flip from false to true, bringing pass_rate from 0.833 to 1.0. No token impact expected (same number of steps). No regression risk for passing tasks since those have non-null funding values.
